cases.note: A second open sees what the first wrote before it lands, as a write is seen at once; the sync lands it on the mount before the close, which the cat after the close reads.

program.python:
import os
fd = os.open('/data/s.txt', os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC)
os.write(fd, b'synced')
os.fsync(fd)
print(open('/data/s.txt').read())
os.write(fd, b'!')
os.fdatasync(fd) if hasattr(os, 'fdatasync') else os.fsync(fd)
print(open('/data/s.txt').read())
os.close(fd)
program.node:
const fsp = require('node:fs').promises
const h = await fsp.open('/data/s.txt', 'w')
await h.write('synced')
await h.sync()
console.log(await fsp.readFile('/data/s.txt', 'utf8'))
await h.write('!')
await h.datasync()
console.log(await fsp.readFile('/data/s.txt', 'utf8'))
await h.close()
